labels.note: The OpenAI SDK is instantiated in browser code with dangerouslyAllowBrowser:true (line 5) and apiKey read from import.meta.env.VITE_OPENAI_API_KEY (line 4). Vite inlines VITE_-prefixed vars into the client bundle at build time, so the secret OpenAI key ships to every visitor's browser, where it can be extracted and abused (billing/quota theft).

Chat completions are called directly from the client with no backend, so there is no server-side rate limiting or per-user quota; any visitor holding the browser-exposed key can issue unbounded requests against the account.

notes: Small public Vite + React 19 OpenAI chatbot demo (recall case; NOT authored by us). The primary, unambiguous issue is the client-side LLM key: OpenAI is constructed in the browser with dangerouslyAllowBrowser:true and a VITE_-prefixed key that Vite bundles into shipped JS. No credential value is committed (.env.template holds only a placeholder and .env is gitignored), so this is an llm-key-client architectural exposure rather than exposed-secret. Secondary llm-no-limit label reflects that the direct-from-browser design has no server-side rate/token cap.
